text:
Ryan Shea has become one of the busiest men on the Oilers' blue line in his first season in Edmonton, playing nearly 23 minutes a night after 150 games with Pittsburgh. The workload is the story. He has blocked 39 shots, and at five on five the Oilers have taken 49% of the expected goals (the quality of the chances) with him on, a little over four points better than when he sits. For a 2015 fourth-round pick who came up through the AHL, that is a real role.

The points haven't followed: 7 in 26 games, none on the power play, and 2 in his last ten. Our numbers put his scoring talent around 1.1 points per 60 minutes against the 0.71 he's producing, so some of that is owed. Evolving-Hockey rated his 2025-26 in Pittsburgh at 3.3 wins above replacement, fifth among defensemen, while warning that his results ran ahead of his chances. The thing to watch is whether Edmonton keeps trusting him with top-four minutes as the season wears on.
headline: Ryan Shea's quiet promotion to big minutes
